outcome_measurement: Treatment-policy estimand; percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 68, with multiple imputation for missing week-68 data
group_1_label: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (target dose 2.4 mg) plus lifestyle counseling
group_2_label: Visually identical once-weekly placebo plus lifestyle counseling
evidence_quote: The mean change from baseline in body weight at week 68 was –13.7% in the semaglutide group and −3.2% in the placebo group (estimated difference, −10.5 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], −12.3 to −8.6; P<0.001) (Fig. 1).
extraction_warning: SE_diff was derived from the explicitly reported 95% CI using (−8.6 − [−12.3]) / 3.92 = 0.943877551. Group sizes are randomized/full-analysis-population denominators because the treatment-policy estimand included all randomized participants with multiple imputation. The reported P value is a threshold (P<0.001), so no exact numeric p_value was entered.
_filter_reason: This primary endpoint directly measures percentage body-weight change at week 68 for semaglutide versus placebo.
target_construct: percentage change in body weight from baseline
outcome_family: percentage change in body weight from baseline

paper_title: Effect of Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Daily Liraglutide on Body Weight in Adults With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes: The STEP 8 Randomized Clinical Trial
true_research_question: In adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes, what is the effect of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg for 68 weeks, compared with pooled matched placebo, on percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 68?
author: Rubino et al.
design_type: Randomized, open-label, parallel-group, multicenter phase 3b clinical trial
medium: Once-weekly subcutaneous medication plus diet and physical activity counseling
participant_type: Adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes
outcome_selection_reason: This is the prespecified eligible percentage body-weight-change outcome at week 68, the latest on-treatment assessment in the 6-to-24-month window, for semaglutide versus pooled placebo.
task_or_measure: Treatment-policy estimand at week 68 using ANCOVA with multiple imputation
outcome_name: Percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 68
outcome_measurement: Estimated percentage change from baseline in body weight at week 68 under the treatment-policy estimand
group_1_label: Pooled matched placebo plus diet and physical activity counseling
group_2_label: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg plus diet and physical activity counseling
additional_group_ns: Once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide 3.0 mg: n=127 randomized (excluded active comparator)
evidence_quote: “The mean weight change from baseline was –15.8% with semaglutide vs –6.4% with liraglutide ...; weight change with pooled placebo was –1.9%.” Table 2 reports for semaglutide: “Body weight, % change ... -15.8 (-17.6 to -13.9) [117].” The Results state: “Overall, 92.3% of participants (n = 312) had a week 68 body weight assessment; data were missing for 9 participants in the semaglutide group, 10 in the liraglutide group, and 7 in the placebo group.”
extraction_warning: The paper excerpt does not explicitly report the adjusted semaglutide-versus-pooled-placebo treatment difference or its 95% CI/SE. M_diff was therefore computed as semaglutide minus placebo from the explicitly reported estimated means: -15.8 - (-1.9) = -13.9 percentage points. SE_diff is left null because the required placebo CI/SE or direct contrast CI/SE is not reported. Randomized full-analysis-set denominators were used because the treatment-policy analysis included all randomized participants with multiple imputation; observed week-68 counts were 117 for semaglutide and 78 for placebo.
_filter_reason: Although secondary and with semaglutide listed as group 2, this outcome directly measures percentage body-weight change at week 68 for the target semaglutide-versus-placebo comparison.
target_construct: percentage change in body weight from baseline
outcome_family: percentage change in body weight from baseline
